scores.claim_text: MultiLane JV (MLTP) announced Jan 29, 2026: Teradyne to invest ~$157M for 75% to serve AI Data Center test market; close in 1H 2026.
supports: EDGAR FTS: 'MultiLane' has 12 total hits including TER 10-K 2026-02-19 and TER 10-Q 2026-05-01 (post-announcement disclosure)
scores.M_value: 12 total hits; TER 10-K + 10-Q + historical II-VI/Verifone/Lightwave mentions — consistent with MultiLane being a real long-standing private high-speed I/O test company subsequently being JV'd
scores.interpretation: Subsequent-event disclosure of a planned JV. Real counterparty (MultiLane has external corroboration in pre-2026 filings of unrelated public companies). Pending close — standard subsequent event.

scores.claim_text: 10% equity stake in Technoprobe S.p.A. acquired May 27, 2024 for $524.1M; carrying value $537.1M (Dec 31, 2025); fair value $935.7M.
supports: EDGAR FTS: 'Technoprobe' has 34 total hits — multiple TER 8-Ks (2023-11-08 original deal announcement, 2024-05-31 close, plus 2024/2025 quarterly updates); Technoprobe is a publicly traded Italian probe-card manufacturer
scores.M_value: 34 hits; TER 8-Ks corroborate deal announcement (2023-11), close (2024-05), and ongoing quarterly equity-method updates
scores.interpretation: Real equity-method investment with publicly observable fair-value mark-to-market (>$400M appreciation since purchase). Audited.

supports: EDGAR FTS: 'Quantifi Photonics' has 7 hits, all from Teradyne filings — 10-K (with ex21_1 subsidiaries exhibit confirming Quantifi as subsidiary), 10-Q 2025-08-01, 10-Q 2025-10-30, 10-Q 2026-05-01, 10-K 2025-05-02 Q1
scores.M_value: 7 hits across TER 10-K (incl. subsidiaries exhibit ex21_1) and post-close 10-Qs
scores.interpretation: Real acquisition, consistently disclosed across quarterly filings, listed as legal subsidiary in Exhibit 21.1. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Acquired Infineon's AET test technology + Regensburg team for $18.3M on Jan 31, 2025.
supports: Infineon is a well-known semiconductor company (real Tier-1 IDM); the acquisition is small relative to TER revenue but is consistently disclosed in 10-K business + acquisitions sections
Pension footnote confirms acquired plan from AET ($2.9M obligation, $2.7M assets) — operational integration evidence beyond mere announcement
scores.M_value: Multiple Teradyne filings reference AET / Infineon integration; pension note shows real plan absorbed (concrete operational evidence)
scores.interpretation: Small carve-out, corroborated by Infineon being a Tier-1 named counterparty and by concrete pension-plan absorption in the footnotes. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Robotics restructuring: ~400 employees impacted; $24.3M of $29.4M severance in 2025 charged to Robotics segment.
supports: Footnote Q (Restructuring) explicitly quantifies severance with cash payments ($15.3M paid in 2025) and timing (remaining to be paid through Q3 2026)
scores.interpretation: Concrete, audited disclosure of headcount action — consistent with Robotics revenue declining from $364.8M (2024) to $308.3M (2025) (-15.5% YoY). Stage-ladder interpretation: this is the OPPOSITE of pilots-as-PR — TER is openly disclosing weakness in Robotics segment. Honest disclosure pattern. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Robotics: third consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth in Q4 2025; full-year Robotics revenue $308.3M (-15.5% YoY).
supports: audited revenue disaggregation by segment in financial footnotes
scores.M_value: Robotics $308.3M FY2025 vs $364.8M FY2024 = -15.5%; intra-year sequential growth (Q2->Q3->Q4) is consistent with cyclical trough recovery, not absolute outperformance
scores.interpretation: MODERATE caveat: the headline 'three sequential quarters of growth' is a real sequential-growth fact but obscures that the segment is still down ~15.5% year-over-year and required a ~400-head restructuring. This is the robotics-specific 'sequential growth' framing that hides absolute decline. Not deceptive — both numbers are disclosed — but the narrative emphasis warrants noting. The Universal Robots / MiR robotics business remains real (39 granted UR patents in USPTO ODP) but is in a cyclical/structural slowdown.

scores.claim_text: Returned $778.4M to shareholders ($702.1M buybacks + $76.3M dividends) in 2025; FY net income $554.0M; diluted EPS $3.47.
supports: audited statements of cash flows + EPS computation footnote P
scores.M_value: Buybacks $702.1M; dividends $76.3M; net income $554M; weighted diluted shares 159.7M
scores.interpretation: Capital return exceeds net income (~140%), funded by cash from operations + balance sheet liquidity. Mature-FCF profile typical of established cap-equipment vendors. No distress markers — opposite end of the spectrum from KSCP/SERV pattern. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Real robotics + semiconductor test IP via Teradyne, Universal Robots, and MiR.
supports: USPTO ODP: Teradyne 488 total applications, 134 granted patents pre-cutoff with semiconductor-test-relevant titles (probe card cooling, DUT communication, etc.)

USPTO ODP: Universal Robots 53 applications, 39 granted patents pre-cutoff with robot-arm-relevant titles (robot element illuminating ring, robot arm cap, robot system configuration, extendable safety system)
scores.M_value: Teradyne n_granted=134; Universal Robots n_granted=39 — both well above heuristic-8 PASS threshold (>=10 with claimed-technology hit). UR patents are clearly in collaborative-robot / cobot domain (arms, safety, configuration).
scores.interpretation: Strong, multi-decade IP portfolios in both semiconductor-test and collaborative-robotics. UR patent topics match the claimed product domain (collaborative robotic arms). PASS — opposite of the Nikola pattern.
